10.1002_adfm.76149: Reducing catalyst dimensions to the nanoscale is effective to obtain high activity, but raises challenges to integrate them into effective and stable catalysts for macroscopic applications. Herein, we report an amorphous CrO x “nano‐glue” to bind CoP nanoparticles into a stable and efficient monolithic structure for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). With the interfacial interaction and charge transfer, the CrO x nano‐glue not only consolidates the nanoparticles to ensure structural stability but also actively promotes the water dissociation, as observed by in situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy and Raman experiments. Consequently, this nano‐glue‐integrated catalyst delivers an outstanding performance in HER, showing a low overpotential of 190 mV (133 mV at 60°C) to achieve the industrial level current density of 1000 mA cm −2 , and can continuously work at this current for over 2000 h. Moreover, it can stably operate in the alkaline seawater at 1000 mA cm −2 for over 1000 h (overpotential of 201 mV). When integrated into a noble‐metal‐free anion exchange membrane cell as the cathode, it can also acquire 1 A cm −2 at 1.63 V (at 80°C) and stably work for over 500 h.
10.1002_anie.202522184: The structure of solution additives significantly affects the polarization and dendrite behavior of metal batteries. In this study, we propose, for the first time, the "hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB) value-spatial configuration synergistic regulation" strategy by selecting cations with different structures as additives, successfully revealing the structure-activity relationship between additive structures and the stability of the anode interface adsorption layer. Among them, the butyltrimethylammonium chloride additive (ADD4), which has a low HLB value and a linear structure, exhibits the most stable interfacial structure. The stable hydrophobic region formed by its spontaneous aggregation and assembly shows a repulsive effect on hydrated protons. The constructed protective layer can effectively reduce overpotential and inhibit the formation of by-products. The battery with ADD4 exhibits excellent stability, with over 1700 cycles and an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.7%. The full laboratory cells and pouch cells can also maintain very good cyclability, verifying their feasibility for practical applications. This study emphasizes that exploring the relationship between the hydrophilic-hydrophobic properties, microstructure of additive ions, and the stability of the adsorption layer is crucial for designing appropriate electrolyte-electrode interface layers.
10.1002_eem2.70456: Catalysts capable of degrading pollutants without external oxidants are pivotal for sustainable environmental remediation. In this study, iron single atoms anchored on N‐doped carbon with pyridinic nitrogen vacancies (Fe‐SAs/N V ‐C) are synthesized for external oxidant‐free pollutant degradation. The optimized Fe‐SAs/N V ‐C catalyst achieves complete removal of ciprofloxacin (CIP) within 1 min, significantly outperforming N‐doped carbon (with only 70% removal) and attains a total organic carbon mineralization ratio of 75.6% within 15 min. The catalyst maintains excellent activity in high‐salinity solution (500 m M NaCl) and under continuous‐flow operation. Kelvin probe force microscopy measurements confirm a shift in surface potential from 25 to −70 mV. Theoretical calculations reveal that pyridinic N V render the Fe SAs and adjacent C sites more electron‐deficient. These features enable the Fe‐SAs/N V ‐C to efficiently extract electrons from CIP, thereby initiating its self‐oxidation. Concurrently, dissolved oxygen accepts electrons from electron‐rich sites on both the catalyst and CIP, generating singlet oxygen that further promotes the degradation. This work provides new insights into the oxidant‐free degradation mechanism mediated by the synergy of electron‐deficient and electron‐rich sites.
10.1002_smll.74727: Multifunctional electrochromic (EC) materials integrating optical modulation, energy storage, and thermal management are vital for next‐generation smart windows. Overcoming the challenge of achieving high transparency, structural precision, and redox stability in a single polymer, we report a gelation‐free hyperbranched conjugated poly(fluorene‐ alt ‐triphenylamine) ( P(Fl‐ alt ‐TPA) ) with a 100% degree of branching (DB). Synthesized via Suzuki–Miyaura polycondensation, it achieves high molecular weight without gelation, thereby overcoming the limitations of conventional A 2 + B 3 . An electrochromic supercapacitor based on this polymer exhibits high energy and power densities, successfully powering an LED and a timer for over 5 and 6 min, respectively. Remarkably, it maintains 80.6% capacity retention after 10 000 cycles. Furthermore, in device applications, it demonstrates pronounced NIR heat‐shielding (achieving a CR NIR of 91.9% and suppressing a water temperature rise by 60.7%) and distinct electrofluorochromism (with a contrast ratio of 177). These results highlight that precise engineering of high‐molecular‐weight hyperbranched conjugated polymers (CPs) without gelation effectively integrates transparency, electrochromism, energy storage, heat shielding, and fluorescence switching into a single platform for advanced smart windows and multifunctional optoelectrochemical applications.
10.1002_smll.74824: This study demonstrates giant capacitive energy storage in Sr‐doped BaTiO 3 ‐CeO 2 (B 1‐ x S x T‐C, 0.0 ≤ x ≤ 1.0) lead‐free epitaxial films via a simple compositional design. By systematically tuning Sr doping level, the polarization behavior of B 1‐ x S x T‐C films transforms from relaxor ferroelectric to super‐paraelectric state, achieving optimized polarization behavior with large maximum polarization, low remnant polarization, and high breakdown strength. Structural analysis reveals that Sr doping induces disordered local structures, forming mixed‐phase nanodomains with local symmetry breaking, suppressing hysteresis while maintaining high polarization. The Sr doping significantly enhances the energy storage efficiency ( η ) of BaTiO 3 ‐based films from ∼ 80% to ∼ 90%, while simultaneously boosting the energy storage density ( U e ) from 57.6 J/cm 3 to 81.2 J/cm 3 . Specially, at x = 0.8, the film achieves a high η of ∼ 85% and a superior U e of 81.2 J/cm 3 . Remarkably, all B 1‐ x S x T‐C films exhibit excellent frequency stability (10 Hz—2 kHz) and thermal stability (25°C–160°C), demonstrating their reliability and stability in energy storage applications. This work provides a practical strategy for designing compositionally optimized and environmentally friendly energy storage films.
10.1016_j.ecoleng.2025.107886: Nature-based solutions are increasingly recognized as effective and multifunctional components of climate-resilient flood protection. While tropical mangroves have received substantial attention, temperate riparian forests, particularly willow systems, offer comparable wave attenuation and biodiversity benefits, yet remain understudied. This study assesses the ecological and protective value of three types of willow floodplain forests: a so-called wild-grown willow forest, a pollard willow forest, and a willow plantation. Using field data from the Biesbosch National Park (the Netherlands), we quantified forest structure, ground-dwelling invertebrate diversity, and modelled wave attenuation under storm scenarios. Structural complexity and biodiversity were highest in the wild-grown forest, with significantly greater invertebrate order richness, larger body sizes, and more heterogeneous canopy architecture. The pollard forest showed the highest wave attenuation efficiency due to their dense, low-lying crown structures. The plantation forest showed lower values across both axes. We integrated these findings into a trade-off model evaluating ecological value, flood protection efficiency, and a 50-year simple cost analysis of each forest type as a hybrid solution alongside traditional dikes. While the pollard forest is the most spatially efficient for flood attenuation, the wild-grown system provides greater ecological value at lower lifecycle cost. Our results underscore the importance of tailoring hybrid flood defense strategies to local priorities - balancing biodiversity, spatial constraints, and economic feasibility. The framework developed here can inform ecosystem-based design in delta regions worldwide, supporting integrated climate adaptation that aligns safety with ecological resilience. • Wild-grown willow forest had highest invertebrate diversity and forest complexity. • Pollard forest attenuated waves most successful. • Pollard forest required 150 m, plantation & wild-grown forest 500 m for safety needs. • Trade-off model showed: hybrid flood defenses economically and ecologically superior.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123064: Engineering MXene-based composites has become a strategic approach to overcoming kinetic limitations, volume expansion, and sluggish multivalent ion diffusion in advanced battery chemistries. Owing to their metallic conductivity, tunable interlayer spacing, redox-active surfaces, and chemically versatile terminations, MXenes transcend the traditional role of conductive additives and function as electrochemical regulators that govern ion transport, interfacial stability, and structural evolution. This review systematically analyzes the design principles, synthesis strategies, and mechanistic roles of MXene-based composites across Li + , Na + , K + , Mg 2+ , and Zn 2+ battery chemistries. It correlates synthesis methodologies including hydrothermal, solvothermal, CVD, ALD, electrochemical deposition, self-assembly, and mechanochemical routes with structural engineering outcomes such as interlayer expansion, heterostructure formation, and defect modulation. Emphasis is placed on the thermodynamic and redox origins of charge storage, distinguishing redox-active versus redox-silent MXenes and positioning these materials along the capacitor-battery continuum. In multivalent systems, MXenes mitigate sluggish kinetics and dendrite formation through interfacial ion regulation and uniform nucleation control, while in monovalent systems they buffer volume expansion and accelerate charge transfer. By integrating conductive scaffolding, ion hosting, and interphase engineering within a single material platform, MXene-based composites offer a unifying strategy for high-rate, high-capacity, and long-life batteries. This review concludes by identifying critical challenges in stability, oxidation resistance, scalable synthesis, and mechanistic ambiguity, and proposes future research directions aimed at realizing MXenes as central components of sustainable post‑lithium energy storage technologies.
10.1021_acsnano.5c13027: The rational design of high-performance metal–organic framework (MOF) membranes for sustainable saline wastewater treatment remains a critical challenge in addressing global water scarcity. Herein, we report an ultrathin zeolitic imidazolate frameworks-8 (ZIF-8) membrane with precisely engineered missing-linker defects, fabricated through a dual metal source strategy, followed by controlled ligand thermolysis. This process precisely introduces missing-linker defects while minimizing the intercrystalline voids. The resultant architecture, characterized by enhanced water affinity, enlarged effective pore apertures, coupled with reduced membrane thickness, enables ultrafast molecular transport, achieving ultrahigh water permeance of 122.5 L m –2 h –1 bar –1 while maintaining near-complete dye rejection (>99.8%). Notably, the membrane exhibits minimal NaCl rejection (9.4%), yielding a salt/dye separation factor of 303.2, surpassing all reported nanofiltration membranes. This work establishes controlled defect engineering as a powerful strategy to overcome the permeability-selectivity trade-off, providing a promising platform for single-step purification of dye-contaminated saline streams.
10.1039_d5ta06749a: This study challenges HOMO level engineering approaches to SAM design by demonstrating that this leads to reduced quasi-Fermi level splitting in the perovskite and thus lower open-circuit voltage and performance.
10.1039_d6gc01980c: Agricultural biomass from corn can be upcycled into valuable biodegradable materials such as zein, ethyl lactate, and membranes, reducing depleting resource consumption, minimizing waste, and contributing to a circular bioeconomy.
